senses.gloss: ch. same.—Pa. בַּזֵּק to cast (or shoot) a mass of fragments (as from a catapult).
units: <cite ref="Sanhedrin 108b">Snh. 108ᵇ</cite> <he>ב׳ בהון עפרא וכ׳</he> Ar. (ed. <he>והוה שדינן</he>) he shot at them with dust and it turned into swords &c. *<cite ref="Bava Batra 73a">B. Bath. 73ᵃ</cite> <he>והוה כי מבזק ארבעין גירוי דברזלא</he> and there was a flash as if one shot forty arrows of iron (v. Koh. Ar. Compl. s. v. <he>בזק</he>, note 5).—Ed. <he>כי מבזר ארב׳ גריוי דחרדלא</he> like one scattering forty measures of mustard [from a confusion of which two versions the variants in Mss. a. in Ar. arose, v. Rabb. D. S. a. l. note.—Ar. <he>כמיבזק</he> Ithpe.].

Yoma 22ᵇ how do you know that Bazek (I Sam. XI, 8, v. next w.) is here used לישנא דמיבזיק in the sense of being broken (a fragment of pottery); perhaps it is the name of a place? B. Bath. 73ᵃ Ar., v. supra.
